$comment: Performance budgets (M-035). Milliseconds, compared against the median of
a `bun run bench` run at the same scale.
These are ceilings, not targets. Each is roughly 2x the measured baseline
on the reference machine (see plans/architecture/08_PERFORMANCE.md), which
is wide enough that a slower laptop or a busy CI runner does not fail, and
tight enough that an algorithmic regression does. A budget failure means
'something changed shape, go look', not 'this machine is slow'.
Raise a budget only with a note in the performance doc saying why the work
got more expensive. Silently widening the ceiling turns this file into
dependency_graph and cycles are the exception: they read a graph indexing
already built, so they measure a memo hit rather than a build. Their
ceilings are deliberately far below the build cost, so that a broken memo
shows up here rather than as a diffuse slowdown everywhere else.

reference.note: Apple Silicon laptop, 2026-08-05. Absolute numbers are machine-dependent; the shape of the scaling is not.
